Location: Zoom

---
Summary: Intro discovery for Reserved (Dedicated) GPUs. BlueTide is evaluating Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private/on-prem; main concerns are tenant isolation, predictable burst handling for weekend job spikes, encryption/KMS and auditability. They want a path for phased approach: start hosted for dev, Dedicated reserve for prod, possible on-prem later for sensitive workloads.
Topics: capacity sizing, warm-pool/prewarm strategy, tenancy/isolation topology, fallback to hosted, encryption/KMS, SOC2 and audit logs, SLA/latency targets, pricing guardrails.
Action items (recap below).
---
Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving time, quick intros?
[00:06] Alan (BlueTide - CTO): Hi, Alan here, CTO. Priya leads M L at BlueTide, Marcus on infra, Sofia on security, we might jump on questions.
[00:15] Maya: Awesome. Jonah on for deep infra questions and Elena will be touchpoint for onboarding.
[00:20] Jonah (Redwood SE): Hey all.
[00:22] Priya: Hi. Thanks.
[00:24] [00:31] Maya: The goal for today is to understand your production profile and what dedicated/reserved GPU topology would look like. High level - are you thinking dedicated for latency-sensitive inference or for data residency reasons?
[00:45] Alan: Both. We have consumer-facing features where 95th percentile latency and consistency are key. Also some models touch PII and we'd prefer private control eventually. But we want to do this in phases; not rip out hosted immediately.
[01:01] Jonah: Makes total sense. Can you walk us through traffic patterns? peaks, baseline, and burst events?
[01:08] Priya: Baseline is about 120 qps across our endpoints during weekday hours, peaks up to 2.2k qps for a 20-30 minute window during promotional events. Also nightly batch reranks that need GPU for re-encoding, but those are less latency sensitive.
[01:26] Marcus: And our burst pattern is weird — it often happens on weekends when marketing blasts run, and we don't want the app to slow down.
[01:33] Jonah: Ok that helps. For Dedicated, we model two things: steady reserved pools sized to hit your baseline and a warm/partial prewarm or burst guard that either uses spare capacity in Dedicated or falls back to Redwood hosted model variants when Dedicated saturates.
[01:50] Maya: One callout — warm pool sizing can hugely affect cost. If you prewarm to cover 2k qps, you pay for that reserved capacity 24/7. But if you use a smaller hotpool plus hosted fallback you can balance cost vs latency.
[02:03] Priya: Host fallback — can you explain the latency implications? If we route to hosted during bursts, what's the extra tail?
[02:12] Jonah: Typically adding a hosted fallback adds a small network hop and possibly a lighter-weight model variant. In our internal benchmarks we see an extra ~20-80 ms depending on region and seq length. For P95 this can be noticeable. Also depends on whether you keep a thin warm lane in Dedicated and send overflow to hosted.
[02:29] [02:37] Sofia (Security): From our side, we need to understand encryption at rest, KMS integration, and audit logs per request. Will data be egressed to hosted if fallback occurs? That's a compliance question for us.
[02:49] Maya: Great question. If you configure a hosted fallback, by default requests will go to Redwood hosted endpoints in the region — that does cross our hosted boundary, and we can sign a data handling addendum, but for strict data residency you can instead configure a hot spare within your Dedicated estate or enable private deployment later. We flagged that in our docs but we'll share specific language in the security pack.
[03:10] [03:19] Jonah: Also, there's an option to route only non-PII traffic to hosted. You can do token-level filtering and have the Dedicated route for PII. It's a config tradeoff.
[03:26] Marcus: For network we run in a VPC and use private peering, we'd need VPC connectors for the Dedicated nodes and for private/on-prem. Do you support Bring-Your-Own-Key for encryption?
[03:38] Maya: Yes, BYOK via KMS/HSM integrations is supported on Private and Dedicated. Hosted supports provider-managed keys by default and customer-managed keys for enterprise plans. We'll share the KMS integration doc.
[03:49] Priya: Let's talk model quant and perf—we run a 13B tuned model. Any guidance on quantization and sequence length tuning?
[03:57] Jonah: For a 13B model we often recommend 4-bit quant or bfloat depending on kernel support. The runtime chooses kernels based on seq length distribution—if your live traffic is 64 tokens typical, that can be optimized differently than 512 token batch reranks. We'll want sample prompts to build a perf profile.
[04:16] Alan: Is there a recommended approach for having two topologies: prod on Dedicated and dev on hosted? What's the rollout pattern?
[04:24] Maya: Many customers start dev on hosted then promote to Dedicated for prod. We support model pinning and rollout policies so you can A/B or canary across environments. Also cost-awareness tools help you see token-level spend by route.
[04:36] [04:41] Priya: For the Dedicated plan, what's the SLA on throughput and preemption? If we reserve nodes, can they be reclaimed?
[04:49] Jonah: Reserved capacity means those GPUs are yours; no preemption. Burst capacity and autoscale are configurable—depending on the agreement we can have burst pools or on-demand spare capacity. For strict isolation you can buy node-level isolation (segregated nodes) which fully fences tenant workloads.
[05:05] Marcus: Segregated nodes — what's the overhead? We worry about underutilization.
[05:11] Jonah: There's always a utilization vs isolation tradeoff. Segregated gives full isolation but you pay for that headroom. Some customers use lighter tenant fencing with cgroup limits and rely on admission control plus burst fallback to reduce cost. We can run modeling for your profile.
[05:25] Maya: We actually do a cost-vs-SLO modeling exercise — we'll run a simulation based on your qps histogram and we can show bucketed expected cost for prewarm sizes. We'll include that in the pricing doc.
[05:37] [05:45] Sofia: Audit logs — we need per-request traceability and long-term retention for 7 years for regulatory reasons. Is that supported?
[05:52] Elena (CSM): We support configurable log retention. For on-prem and Private you manage storage; for Dedicated we can support extended retention as an add-on. We'll note retention costs.
[06:02] Priya: Can you walk through an example failure mode — e.g., Dedicated saturates during a marketing blast and hosted is also slower — what's the graceful degradation?
[06:14] Jonah: Commonly we provide: (1) rate-limiting rules by route to avoid noisy neighbors, (2) model downgrades — route to a smaller quantized model automatically, (3) queued requests with retry policies, (4) fallback to hosted or to cached responses for frequent prompts. We also instrument per-route SLA alarms.
[06:31] Alan: That model downgrade—what about hallucination/regression risk? We need evaluation hooks.
[06:36] Maya: Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring tied to prompt sets. You can pin evaluation sets and get regression alerts tied to specific model changes. We'll demonstrate that in the follow-up.
[06:48] [07:00] Priya: For benchmarking, we'd like a 48-hour soak with our workload. Can Redwood run that in a Dedicated trial?
[07:07] Jonah: Yes, we can run a bounded trial. Typically we ask for sample prompts and keys, and we'll instrument token-level traces. We can run it in a dedicated staging pool in our infra or set up a Private eval on your infra depending on needs. For early stages hosted trial is fastest, Dedicated trial takes a bit more provisioning.
[07:27] Marcus: Provisioning timeline — how long to stand up Dedicated nodes in our region (us-west-2)?
[07:33] Maya: Typical lead time is 2-4 weeks for Dedicated reservation depending on capacity. If you need on-prem, that adds hardware lead time. We'll send a detailed timeline.
[07:43] Sofia: Certificates and SSO — we require SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for RBAC. Do you integrate?
[07:51] Maya: Yes SAML/SSO and SCIM are supported for enterprise. We'll attach our SSO guide.
[07:58] [08:05] Priya: Pricing question — do you price by reserved vCPU/GPU or by token spend on top? We need predictable unit economics.
[08:14] Maya: Dedicated is typical reserved monthly commit for GPU pools and included bandwidth. We also surface token-level accounting for engineering teams. Add-ons like extended retention and premium SLA are priced separately. We'll include a few example scenarios.
[08:28] [08:35] Alan: Competitors we've looked at either lock you into a bigger reserve or don't offer private deployments. We liked Redwood's model selection and the observability features. Concern is cost at scale.
[08:45] Jonah: That's why we model the warm-pool vs fallback trade—many customers save 30-60% by tuning prewarm to baseline and letting hosted cover spikes. But for strict latency/P95 needs customers provision more reserved headroom.
[08:58] [09:10] Priya: A few technical specifics — do you expose KV cache management hooks? We rely heavily on KV cache reuse across sessions for chat style flows.
[09:20] Jonah: We do. The runtime manages KV cache; you can pin session affinity to a node if you need warm KV. For cross-node affinity we rely on the caching layer and continuous batching. We'll show config examples.
[09:35] Marcus: Can we do tenant-aware prewarming? e.g., only prewarm models for premium customers or for specific routes?
[09:42] Maya: Yes route-level prewarm policies are supported — you can prioritize high-value tenants. That reduces cost.
[09:48] [09:55] Sofia: For compliance, we want to ensure logs cannot be deleted accidentally and that there are immutable audit trails. Is write-once storage an option?
[10:03] Elena: For Dedicated and Private deployments we can support append-only logs and integration with your archival storage; we'll list options in the security pack.
[10:12] Maya: We're going to propose two phased options: (A) Hosted dev -> Dedicated reserved for prod with small warm pool + hosted overflow; (B) Hosted dev -> Dedicated prod with segregated nodes sized for 90% of peak and a contractual burst pool for the remaining 10% (more expensive but strict isolation).
[10:34] Priya: Which option do you recommend?
[10:36] Jonah: For your traffic profile — baseline 120 qps, spikes ~2.2k qps for short bursts — the cost-optimal approach is Option A: size Dedicated for steady state and overnight batch, keep a thin hotpool for critical P95 routes, and use hosted overflow for ephemeral spikes. If you have strict regulatory windows then Option B is better.
[10:56] [11:05] Alan: We need the pricing math to show to finance. Also want to know contractual SLAs and what credits look like if you miss latency SLO.
[11:13] Maya: We'll include SLA language and example credit calculations. For Dedicated enterprise we offer an SLA backing uptime and latency with a remediation playbook.
[11:24] Marcus: On the instrumentation side, can we get per-token cost and latency traces into our observability stack? We use Datadog.
[11:33] Elena: Yes we have tracing hooks and Datadog exporters; we can show sample dashboards.
[11:39] [11:45] Priya: Any notes on model rollout during bursts? Suppose we deploy a new model and traffic surges at the same time — how to avoid regression?
[11:53] Jonah: Use canary rollouts, small percent routes, and Redwood Optimize regression alerts tied to your eval prompts. You can also schedule rollouts outside typical peak windows.
[12:06] [12:10] Alan: Are there any hard limits on concurrency per node? We need to calculate how many GPUs to reserve.
[12:17] Jonah: Concurrency per GPU depends on model size and token length. For a 13B model with 64 token average, one A100-equivalent node can handle X concurrent streams — we'll run exact sims in our sizing workbook. Send us the seq length histogram and we'll populate the model.
[12:38] Priya: We'll share those histograms.
[12:41] [12:45] Maya: Ok last section, next steps and owners. We'll send a Dedicated pricing deck with scenario modeling, SOC2/security pack, and a benchmark plan. Jonah will propose a 48-hour soak plan and a failure-mode diagram. BlueTide to provide traffic histogram, SLOs, and list of PII routes.
[12:58] Alan: Sounds good. Any immediate blockers?
[13:01] Sofia: We need specific contract language around data handling if fallback to hosted is used.
[13:06] Maya: We'll include that as an addendum.
[13:09] [13:15] Priya: One last weird thing: our rerank batch sometimes has 5k long sequence tokens per request — will that change recommended node sizing?
[13:24] Jonah: Yes long sequence reranks push memory footprint up. For batch reranks we might dedicate separate nodes tuned for long sequences and use quant to save memory. We'll model those costs separately.
[13:36] Maya: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and pricing.
[13:42] Alan: Thanks.
[13:44] Priya: Thanks all.
[13:46] [End of recording]
---
Recap (brief):
- BlueTide wants phased approach: dev hosted -> prod Dedicated -> consider Private/on-prem for PII workloads.
- Key constraints: P95 latency, weekend burst up to ~2.2k qps, long-seq batch reranks, SOC2/log retention, KMS/BYOK.
- Recommended: size Dedicated for steady-state, small hotpool per-route, hosted overflow for spikes (cost-optimal), or segregated nodes for strict isolation (costly).
